subject: Urgent: emergency runtime patch and forced-failover coordination
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Julian Hart <julian.hart@brightmetrics.com>, support@brightmetrics.com
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: emergency runtime patch and forced-failover coordination

Hi Julian / BrightMetrics team —

Quick note to let you know we discovered an unexpected memory regression in the 1.2.x runtime path that can, under high-concurrency 8k+ token workloads, cause process instability and elevated error rates. We are pushing an emergency patch to reduce the regression surface, but that patch requires a rolling restart or a brief forced-failover for a subset of serving pods in your dedicated pool.

Planned actions (short notice):
- Immediate: Roll out runtime patch 1.2.9 to a canary subset (10% of traffic) starting at 12:00 PM PDT.
- Contingency: If canary shows elevated errors, we will initiate a forced-failover to healthy variant (1.1.4) for affected shards. Expected disruption: brief connection resets (~10–30s per connection) for affected requests.
- Follow-up: full rollback or progressive rollout depending on telemetry; we will keep you notified.

Attachments: we attached relevant service logs and the patch notes for transparency.

Ask: please confirm whether BrightMetrics has any high-priority jobs scheduled in the 12:00–14:00 PDT window that we should avoid. If you prefer, we can wait for a pre-approved maintenance window but that will delay mitigation.

I’ll be on the thread and reachable on Slack (connor) and phone. Apologies for the short notice — we pushed this because we observed error amplification on production traffic.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Escalations Lead | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: service-logs-20270509.txt (text), patch-release-notes-1.2.9.pdf (pdf)

From: Julian Hart <julian.hart@brightmetrics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@brightmetrics.com
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: emergency runtime patch and forced-failover coordination

Connor —

Thanks for the heads up. We do have a morning batch of nightly analytics jobs that spike CPU between 12:30–13:15 PDT, but they’re lower business priority and can be paused if needed.

Please go ahead with the canary at 12:00 PM. Two asks:
1) Can you set the canary on non-critical shards that don’t serve real-time customer-facing endpoints?
2) Share the rollback criteria (error thresholds / SLO breaches) so our on-call knows when to escalate.

I’ll have our SRE, Maya Lopez, on standby (cc not included here to keep thread narrow).

—Julian
Director of Platform Engineering | BrightMetrics
julian.hart@brightmetrics.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Julian Hart <julian.hart@brightmetrics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: emergency runtime patch and forced-failover coordination

Julian / Connor —

Status update and operational plan (canary at 12:00 PM initiated as requested):

Observations so far:
- Canary rollout began at 12:01 PM PDT to 14 nodes (non-production-labeled shards). No crash loops seen in first 15 minutes, but we observed transient 502/504 spikes between 12:05–12:12 correlating to KV-cache misses on 8k+ token requests. Detailed logs attached.

Rollback / failover criteria (what will trigger forced-failover to 1.1.4):
- >= 3x increase in 5m error-rate compared to baseline AND sustained for 3 consecutive 5m windows, OR
- Any crash loop / OOM observed on >1% of canary nodes, OR
- Latency p50 degradation > 250ms AND customer-facing request error rate increases >1%

If criteria met, immediate steps:
1) Initiate forced-failover of affected shards to variant 1.1.4 (expected ~30s connection resets per pod).
2) Throttle incoming traffic to affected shards by 50% for 10 minutes to allow KV-cache reseeding.
3) Open RINF-8452 (Jira) for post-incident root cause analysis and follow-up.

We have pushed patch-release-notes-1.2.9.pdf and service-logs-20270509.txt to the thread; runbook is at the shared drive link.

We’ll keep telemetry channel open (PagerDuty incident P4642) and will post real-time metrics to the status page.

—David
Senior SRE, Runtime Reliability | Redwood Inference

On Sun, May 9, 2027 at 12:03 PM Julian Hart <julian.hart@brightmetrics.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads up. We do have a morning batch of nightly analytics jobs...

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Julian Hart <julian.hart@brightmetrics.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 15:06:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Urgent: emergency runtime patch and forced-failover coordination

Julian —

Thanks for the quick reply and flexibility on the batch window. Canary finished at 14:00 with the following conclusion:
- Canary passed: no OOMs, no persistent crash loops. We did see short-lived proxy resets between 12:05–12:12 during KV-cache reseed but those fell within rollback thresholds.
- No forced-failover required. We will proceed with a progressive rollout to an additional 40% of nodes starting 15:30 PDT, with the option to pause and fail back if we hit the thresholds above.

Post-actions:
- RINF-8452 opened (link above) for RCA.
- We’ll publish a short customer-facing postmortem in 48 hours and share mitigation guidance for heavy 8k+ token workloads (recommended batching + prefix-caching tips).

Appreciate the quick coordination — I’ll post again when the 40% rollout is complete.

Best,
Connor
Account Escalations Lead | Redwood Inference
